sentences.text: The lingual crown uvula on its teeth shows variable development, being less pronounced than in most Protoplatyrhina renae specimens.
Protoplatyrhina bourdoni was introduced as a new species in a 2026 paper in The Anatomical Record authored by Benjamin Spencer Goode.
The species was formally described by Goode, who erected the name based on teeth recovered from the Hosta Tongue of the Point Lookout Sandstone in New Mexico, USA.
The type locality for the species is the Point Lookout Sandstone formation in New Mexico.
Protoplatyrhina belongs to the subclass of cartilaginous fishes, Chondrichthyes.
Within that class it is placed in the parent group Rhinobatoidei.
A new family, Protoplatyrhinidae, was created to contain Protoplatyrhina and related taxa.
Fossils of the genus are known from the Turonian to Maastrichtian interval, about 93.9 to 66 million years ago.
These remains were found in the United States, specifically in New Mexico.
The species lived during the Cretaceous period.
Researchers consider the phylogenetic position of Protoplatyrhina to be contested.
